title: The second step of the money: firms paid by three or more City-funded nonprofits
question: Which for-profit firms receive money from three or more City-funded nonprofits, and are they tied to the nonprofits or to City politics in any other way?
finding: 23 firms are named as a largest contractor, landlord or grant recipient on the tax returns of three or more City-funded nonprofits, receiving $129.8 million in all. 9 are audit, payroll, insurance or similar firms that serve many clients by nature; of the other 14, the one with most paying nonprofits is Block by Block (5 nonprofits, $17.6 million). 5 are also paid by the City directly, 10 have staff who gave to local campaigns, none pays registered lobbyists, and none shares an address or an officer's name with a nonprofit that pays it.
how: Tax returns of the organizations profiled in this project list their five highest-paid outside contractors each year (Form 990 Part VII, Section B) and their grants to organizations (Schedule I). Payee names were normalised and counted across paying nonprofits; rows whose service is rent or a lease are marked landlord; grant recipients are counted only where the return gives a company type. Left out: payees that read as an individual's name, City-funded nonprofits and anything in the IRS list of California exempt organizations. City payments are the ledger total for the same name, fiscal 2019 to 2026. Campaign gifts are contributions by people who name the firm as employer in the Ethics Commission's transaction file; lobbying is what registered lobbyists report receiving from it. Specialist suppliers are listed first, then firms of a kind that serves many clients by nature.
limits: Being linked is not being involved: nonprofits share board members, buildings and auditors all the time, and San Francisco is a small city. A group is a place to look, ranked by how many independent signs sit inside it. A return lists only the five largest contractors over $100,000, so a firm paid less, or sixth, is invisible, and three is a floor. A good cleaning, security or staffing firm is hired by many nonprofits for ordinary reasons, and nonprofits share auditors all the time. A name match across returns can join two different firms with the same name; a firm under two names is counted twice. Pays (grant, contract or rent): sub-grants and specialist contractors are how programmes are delivered. Same street address: nonprofit centres, landlords and tenants, and fiscal sponsors share buildings. Gives to the campaign of: campaign donations are reported, with limits on amounts. Lobbies or consults for: lobbying and permit consulting are registered and reported.
